1.1: The song of songs, which is Shelomoh’s.
1.2:
Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth, 
For your loves are better than wine.
1.3:
For fragrance your oils are good. 
Your name is oil poured forth, therefore the maidens love you.
1.4:
Draw me! We run after you. 
The meleḵ has brought me into his inner rooms. 
We exult and rejoice in you. 
We praise your loves more than wine. 
Rightly do they love you.
1.5:
I am dark, but lovely, 
O daughters of Yerushalayim, 
Like the tents of Qĕḏar, 
Like the curtains of Shelomoh.
1.6:
Do not look upon me, because I am dark, 
Because the sun has tanned me. 
My mother’s sons were displeased with me. 
They made me the keeper of the vineyards, 
My own vineyard I have not kept.
1.7:
Make known to me, O you whom my being loves, 
Where you pasture, 
Where you rest them at noon. 
For why should I be as one who is veiled 
Beside the flocks of your companions?
1.8:
If you do not know, O fairest among women, 
Go in the footsteps of the flock, 
And feed your little goats beside the shepherds’ dwellings.
1.9:
I have compared you, my love, 
To my filly among Pharaoh’s chariots.
1.10:
Your cheeks are pretty with ornaments, 
Your neck with strings of beads.
1.11:
Let us make you ornaments of gold 
With studs of silver.
1.12:
While the meleḵ is at his table, 
My nard shall give its fragrance.
1.13:
My beloved is a bundle of myrrh to me, 
Lying between my breasts.
1.14:
My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blooms 
In the vineyards of Ĕyn Geḏi.
1.15:
See, you are lovely, my love! 
See, you are lovely! 
Your eyes are as doves.
1.16:
See, you are handsome, my beloved! 
Even pleasant! 
Also our bed is green.
1.17:
The beams of our houses are cedar, 
Our rafters are of fir.

2.1:
I am the rose of Sharon, 
The lily of the valleys.
2.2:
Like a lily among thorns, 
So is my love among the daughters.
2.3:
Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, 
So is my beloved among the sons. 
I delighted in his shade and sat down, 
And his fruit was sweet to my taste.
2.4:
He brought me to the house of wine, 
And his banner over me was love.
2.5:
“Strengthen me with raisin cakes, 
Refresh me with apples, 
For I am faint with love.”
2.6:
His left hand is under my head, 
And his right hand embraces me.
2.7:
I have put you under oath, 
O daughters of Yerushalayim, 
By the gazelles or by the does of the field, 
Do not stir up nor awaken love until it pleases.
2.8:
The voice of my beloved! 
See, he is coming, 
Leaping on the mountains, 
Skipping on the hills.
2.9:
My beloved is like a gazelle or like a young stag. 
See, he is standing behind our wall, 
Looking through the windows, 
Peering through the lattice.
2.10:
My beloved responded and said to me, 
“Rise up, my love, 
My lovely one, and come away.
2.11:
“For look, the winter is past, 
The rain is over, gone.
2.12:
“The flowers have appeared in the earth; 
The time of singing has come, 
And the voice of the turtledove 
Is heard in our land.
2.13:
“The fig tree has ripened her figs, 
And the vines with the tender grapes have given a good fragrance. 
Rise up, my love, 
My lovely one, and come away!
2.14:
“O my dove, in the clefts of the rock, 
In the covering of the cliff, 
Let me see your appearance, 
Let me hear your voice; 
For your voice is sweet, 
And your appearance is lovely.”
2.15:
Catch the foxes for us, 
The little foxes that spoil the vines, 
And our vines are in blossom.
2.16:
My beloved is mine, and I am his. 
He feeds among the lilies.
2.17:
Until the day breaks and the shadows have fled, 
Turn, my beloved, 
And be like a gazelle or a young stag 
On the mountains of Bether.

3.2:
“Come, let me arise, and go about the city, 
In the streets and in the broad places 
I seek the beloved of my being.” 
I sought him, but I did not find him.
3.3:
The watchmen who go about the city found me, to whom I said, 
“Have you seen the beloved of my being?”
3.4:
Scarcely had I passed by them, 
When I found the beloved of my being. 
I held him and would not let him go, 
Until I had brought him to the house of my mother, 
And into the room of her who conceived me.
3.5:
I have put you under oath, 
O daughters of Yerushalayim, 
By the gazelles or by the does of the field, 
Do not stir up nor awaken love until it pleases.
3.6:
Who is this coming out of the wilderness 
Like columns of smoke, 
Perfumed with myrrh and frankincense,
3.7:
From all the merchant’s fragrant powders? 
See, it is Shelomoh’s couch - 
Sixty mighty men are around it, 
Of the mighty men of Yisra’ĕl,
3.8:
All of them holding swords, 
Skilled in battle, 
Each one has his sword on his thigh 
Because of fear in the night.
3.9:
Meleḵ Shelomoh made himself 
A palanquin of the wood of Leḇanon;
3.10:
He made its posts of silver, 
Its support of gold, its seat of purple, 
Within it was decked with love 
By the daughters of Yerushalayim.
3.11:
Go forth, O daughters of Tsiyon, 
And see Meleḵ Shelomoh with the crown 
With which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding, 
And on the day of his gladness of heart.

4.1:
See, you are lovely, my love! 
See, you are lovely! 
Your eyes are as doves behind your veil. 
Your hair is like a flock of goats, 
Going down from Mount Gil’aḏ.
4.2:
Your teeth are like a shorn flock 
Which have come up from the washing, 
All of them bear twins, 
And not one loses her young.
4.3:
Your lips are like a cord of scarlet, 
And your speech is lovely. 
Your cheeks behind your veil 
Are like a piece of pomegranate.
4.4:
Your neck is like the tower of Dawiḏ 
Built for an armory, 
On which hang a thousand shields, 
All the armor of mighty men.
4.5:
Your two breasts are like two fawns, 
Twins of a gazelle, 
Pasturing among the lilies.
4.6:
Until the day breaks 
And the shadows have fled, 
I shall go my way to the mountain of myrrh, 
And to the hill of frankincense.
4.7:
You are all lovely, my love, 
And not a blemish is on you.
4.8:
Come with me from Leḇanon, 
My bride, with me from Leḇanon. 
Look from the top of Amanah, 
From the top of Senir and Ḥermon, 
From the dens of lions, 
From the mountains of the leopards.
4.9:
You have put heart into me, 
My sister, my bride; 
You have put heart into me 
With one look from your eyes, 
With one bead of your necklace.
4.10:
How sweet have been your loves, 
My sister, my bride! 
How much better than wine are your loves, 
And the fragrance of your perfumes than all spices!
4.11:
Your lips, O my bride, 
Drip as the honeycomb; 
Honey and milk are under your tongue. 
And the fragrance of your garments 
Is like the fragrance of Leḇanon.
4.12:
A garden locked is my sister, my bride, 
A fountain locked, a spring sealed up.
4.13:
Your plants are an orchard of pomegranates, 
With pleasant fruits, 
With henna, nard,
4.14:
Nard and saffron, 
Calamus and cinnamon, 
With all trees of frankincense, 
Myrrh and aloes, 
With all the chief spices;
4.15:
A garden spring, 
A well of living waters, 
And streams from Leḇanon.
4.16:
Awake, O north wind, 
And come, O south! 
Blow upon my garden, 
Let its spices flow out. 
Let my beloved come to his garden 
And eat its pleasant fruits.

5.2:
I was sleeping, 
But my heart was awake - 
The voice of my beloved! He knocks, 
“Open for me, my sister, 
My love, my dove, my perfect one; 
For my head is drenched with dew, 
My locks with the drops of the night.”
5.3:
I have taken off my robe, 
Should I put it on? 
I have washed my feet, 
Should I dirty them?
5.4:
My beloved put his hand by the latch, 
And my feelings were deeply moved for him.
5.5:
I rose to open for my beloved, 
And my hands dripped with myrrh, 
My fingers with flowing myrrh, 
On the handles of the lock.
5.6:
I opened for my beloved, 
But my beloved had turned away, gone. 
My being went out when he spoke. 
I sought him, but I could not find him; 
I called him, but he gave me no answer.
5.7:
The watchmen found me, 
Who went about the city. 
They struck me, they bruised me; 
The keepers of the walls 
Lifted my veil from me.
5.8:
I have put you under oath, 
O daughters of Yerushalayim, 
If you find my beloved, 
That you inform him 
That I am faint with love!
5.9:
What kind of a beloved is your beloved, 
O fairest among women? 
What kind of a beloved is your beloved, 
That you have put us under oath?
5.10:
My beloved is dazzling and tanned, 
Chief among ten thousand.
5.12:
His eyes are like doves 
By streams of waters, 
Washed with milk, 
And fitly placed.
5.13:
His cheeks are like a bed of spices, 
A raised bed of scented plants. 
His lips are lilies, 
Dripping, flowing myrrh.
5.14:
His hands are rods of gold 
Filled with beryl. 
His body is carved ivory 
Covered with sapphires.
5.15:
His legs are columns of marble 
Founded on sockets of fine gold. 
His appearance is like Leḇanon, 
Choice as the cedars.
5.16:
His mouth is most sweet, 
And he is altogether lovely. 
This is my beloved, and this is my friend, 
O daughters of Yerushalayim!

6.1:
“Where has your beloved gone, 
O fairest among women? 
Where has your beloved turned aside? 
Let us seek him with you.”
6.2:
My beloved went down to his garden, 
To the beds of spices, 
To feed in the gardens, 
And to gather lilies.
6.3:
I am my beloved’s, 
And my beloved is mine. 
He feeds among the lilies.
6.4:
O my love, you are as lovely as Tirtsah, 
Lovely as Yerushalayim, 
Awesome as an army with banners!
6.5:
Turn your eyes away from me, 
Because they overcome me. 
Your hair is like a flock of goats 
That have hopped down from Gil’aḏ.
6.6:
Your teeth are like a flock of sheep 
That have come up from the washing; 
All of them bear twins, 
And not one among them has lost her young.
6.7:
Your cheeks behind your veil 
Are like a piece of pomegranate.
6.8:
There are sixty melaḵoth 
And eighty concubines, 
And innumerable maidens.
6.9:
My dove, my perfect one, 
Is the only one, the only one of her mother, 
The choice of the one who bore her. 
The daughters saw, and called her fortunate, 
Melaḵoth and concubines, 
And they praised her.
6.10:
Who is she who shines forth as the morning 
Lovely as the moon, 
Clear as the sun, 
Awesome as an army with banners?
6.11:
I went down to the garden of nuts 
To see the budding of the wadi, 
To see whether the vine had budded 
And the pomegranates had bloomed.
6.12:
I did not know, 
My desire made me 
As the chariots of my noble people.
6.13:
Return, return, 
O Shulammite; 
Return, return, 
And let us look upon you! 
Why should you look upon the Shulammite, 
As it were the dance of two armies?

7.1:
How lovely are your feet in sandals, 
O daughter of a noble! 
The curves of your thighs are like ornaments, 
The work of a craftsman’s hands.
7.2:
Your navel is a rounded bowl 
Let it not lack mixed wine. 
Your body is a heap of wheat, 
Hedged about with lilies.
7.3:
Your two breasts are like two fawns, 
Twins of a gazelle.
7.4:
Your neck is like an ivory tower, 
Your eyes, pools in Ḥeshbon 
By the gate of Bath Rabbim. 
Your nose is like the tower of Leḇanon 
Looking to Dammeseq.
7.6:
How lovely and how pleasant you are, 
O love, in delights!
7.7:
This stature of yours compares to a palm tree, 
And your breasts to clusters.
7.8:
I said, “Let me go up to the palm tree, 
Let me take hold of its tips.” 
And please, let your breasts be like clusters of the vine, 
And the fragrance of your breath like apples,
7.9:
And your palate like the best wine, 
Going down smoothly for my beloved, 
Flowing gently, slumbering lips.
7.10:
I am my beloved’s, 
And his desire is toward me.
7.12:
Let us get up early to the vineyards; 
Let us see whether the vine has budded, 
The grape blossoms have opened, 
The pomegranates have bloomed. 
There I give you my loves.
7.13:
The love-apples have given fragrance, 
And at our gates are all pleasantries, 
New and old, 
Which I have laid up for you, my beloved.

8.1:
Who would make you a brother to me, 
Who nursed at my mother’s breasts? 
Should I find you outside, 
I would kiss you; 
I would not be despised.
8.2:
I would lead you, 
I would bring you into the house of my mother, 
She who has taught me. 
I would give you spiced wine to drink, 
Of the juice of my pomegranate.
8.3:
His left hand is under my head, 
And his right hand embraces me.
8.4:
I have put you under oath, 
O daughters of Yerushalayim, 
Do not stir up or awake 
Love until it pleases.
8.5:
Who is this coming up from the wilderness, 
Leaning upon her beloved? 
Under the apple tree I awakened you. 
There your mother was in labor with you; 
There she was in labor, gave birth to you.
8.7:
Many waters are unable to extinguish love, 
And floods do not wash it away. 
If one would give all the wealth of his house for love, 
It would be utterly scorned.
8.8:
We have a little sister, 
And she has no breasts. 
What do we do for our sister 
In the day when she is spoken for?
8.9:
If she is a wall, 
We build upon her a battlement of silver. 
And if she is a door, 
We would enclose her with boards of cedar.
8.10:
I am a wall, 
And my breasts like towers; 
So I became in his eyes 
As one who found peace.
8.12:
My own vineyard is before me. 
O Shelomoh, a thousand belongs to you, 
And two hundred to those who keep its fruit.
8.14:
Hurry, my beloved, 
And be like a gazelle or a young stag 
On the mountains of spices.
